mechanism: Slow, limited-attention information diffusion from Bitcoin into smaller altcoins: a large BTC 1h move carries market-wide information (macro, ETF flow, liquidation cascades) that BTC's deeper liquidity and higher trader attention price in almost immediately, but altcoin holders/algos with less continuous monitoring under-react on the same bar and catch up over the following hours, producing same-direction continuation in the alt rather than the instant, fully efficient co-move a frictionless market would show.
counterparty: Altcoin holders and slow-reacting altcoin order flow (lower-attention retail/smaller desks) who do not monitor BTC in real time and are systematically the last to reprice after a BTC shock, handing the diffusion-following side of the trade to whoever reacts first.
prediction: In the hour(s) after a BTC 1h close with |log return| >= 64.4bps (the pre-registered threshold, this run's 90th-percentile |BTC 1h return| in mr_edge train), ETH/SOL/XRP/DOGE 1h-forward returns are same-signed with BTC's shock at a rate and magnitude that clears the 11.5bps round-trip cost; if instead the co-move is already fully priced by the close of BTC's own shock bar (efficient, no diffusion lag), the strategy's net_bps_mean will not differ from zero.

nearest_dead_rows.why_different: Row 2 (alt-vs-ETH short-horizon reversion, high-vol) trades a reversion in an alt-vs-ETH spread and was killed as regime-luck; this thesis trades continuation (not reversion) in a single alt's own price, triggered by an exogenous BTC shock, not a relative-value spread.

Row 5 (market-neutral cross-sectional momentum) needs a 100-470 name long/short basket ranked on trailing returns and died to survivorship/dilution; this thesis is a single-trigger, single-leg directional trade per alt keyed off one specific exogenous BTC event, not a cross-sectional ranking book, so the dilution failure mode that killed row 5 does not apply the same way.

evidence: Guo, Sang, Tu & Wang, "Cross-cryptocurrency return predictability," Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control 163 (2024), article 104863 (SSRN working paper id 3974583, first posted 2022, published 2024). The open abstract, fetched at the Bristol research-information page, states verbatim: 'the lagged returns of other cryptocurrencies serve as significant predictors of focal cryptocurrencies' and 'a long-short portfolio formed on the past returns of cryptocurrencies can generate a sizable return out-of-sample after accounting for transaction costs,' attributing the effect to 'the spillover effect mechanism, where common shocks among cryptocurrencies coupled with the limited attention of investors lead to slow information diffusion across coins.' The abstract text available to me does not carry a specific bps/Sharpe figure (SSRN and ScienceDirect full-text/abstract pages returned 403 when fetched directly, so no numeric figure from the paper itself is cited here — the abstract's own quoted language is the full extent of what I verified, not a fabricated number). To size an honest expected_trades_per_week for this run's spec (exploratory only, not evidence of edge): running research.swarm.lib.load_data.load_ohlcv('BTC','1h',era='train',dataset='mr_edge') and taking the 90th percentile of |1h log return| gives 64.4bps with 170 threshold-crossing bars over the ~10-week train span (17/week) -- script and printed output saved at research/swarm/runs/2026-09-20-0300/exploratory/literature/btc_threshold_probe_output.txt. A separate, unrelated exploratory check (docs/2026-09-16-edge-swarm-v1/sweep/leadlag/local_check.py, re-run read-only, output at research/swarm/runs/2026-09-20-0300/exploratory/literature/local_check_output.txt) found a same-signed pooled 5m BTC-to-next-bar-alt lead-lag effect on 22 symbols from backtest_data_june (mean +1.71bps, se 0.31, n=27216, hit-rate 0.475) -- directionally consistent with the diffusion mechanism but far too small at 5m to clear the 11.5bps cost, which is exactly why this thesis is specified on 1h bars with a large-shock trigger and a multi-hour hold instead of an unconditional 5m signal.

spec.doa_line: Kill if, at first read after n>=30 accumulates (train screen) or after 4 weeks of paper if n<30 by then, the 95% bootstrap CI of net_bps_mean (research.swarm.lib.bootstrap_ci.mean_ci) includes zero, or if observed WR < p_star(150)=53.83% (research.swarm.lib.fee_math.p_star), or if either the tp_bps +20% (180bps) or -20% (120bps) robustness variant flips net_bps_mean sign relative to the registered 150bps run.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from research.swarm.lib import load_data as ld

BTC_THRESHOLD = 0.00644  # 90th pct |BTC 1h log return|, train exploratory probe (mr_edge, train era)


def signals(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Long/short an altcoin the bar after BTC posts a large 1h closed-bar move,
    on the mechanism that altcoins slowly diffuse BTC's information. Uses only
    BTC bars at or before each of df's own bar timestamps (merge_asof backward),
    so truncating df to any prefix cannot change any already-computed value."""
    btc = ld.load_ohlcv("BTC", "1h", era="train", dataset="mr_edge")
    btc_ret = np.log(btc["close"]).diff().rename("btc_ret")
    left = pd.DataFrame({"ts": df.index}).sort_values("ts")
    right = btc_ret.reset_index()
    right.columns = ["ts", "btc_ret"]
    right = right.sort_values("ts")
    merged = pd.merge_asof(left, right, on="ts", direction="backward")
    aligned = pd.Series(merged["btc_ret"].to_numpy(), index=df.index)
    sig = pd.Series(0, index=df.index, dtype=int)
    sig[aligned >= BTC_THRESHOLD] = 1
    sig[aligned <= -BTC_THRESHOLD] = -1
    return sig
